source.title: Beyond Linear Superposition: Discovering Climate Features in AI Weather Models with KAN-SAE

record.tranche_reason: Tests SAE feature discovery in a new setting: a weather-prediction transformer, rather than the LLM setting named in V4. It compares nonlinear and linear SAEs and reports recovered climate features.
record.gate_note: The paper's cited findings about GraphCast are prior work, not results of this study. The reconstruction-fidelity and activation-norm comparisons are not included as rows because they do not measure a claim version. The feature-correlation measurements are included as related evidence, but do not establish the feature geometry specified by a version.
record.test_reason: The paper introduces a new SAE (KAN-SAE) and uses SAEs as a tool on a 20.5M-parameter weather transformer (SONNY). Its quantitative results (Table 1) compare its own method with a linear SAE. Its case studies show interpretable features in a non-LLM forecasting model. None of this measures what a version names in the system that version names: V4 concerns LLMs, and no toy-model, polysemanticity, SAE-canonicity or feature-dimensionality test is run. The title's 'beyond linear superposition' refers to the encoder activation function, not to a test of superposition.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also claim more strongly that nonlinear activations are 'essential' and recover features 'invisible to linear baselines'. They report a Layer-0 to Layer-5 push–pull circuit for F590. They describe reconstruction as comparable despite EV of 84.2% vs 86.6%.
record.recipe_differences: The paper does not reproduce the toy-network experiments in Toy Models of Superposition. It trains nonlinear and linear SAEs on Layer-5 activations from a weather transformer and compares feature metrics and climate case studies.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported feature results differ between KAN-SAE and L IN -SAE; the heatwave feature localization differs substantially, while both methods localize the typhoon feature within 3°. Results are restricted to Layer 5 of one model.

fits_no_version.finding: In a 20.5M-parameter weather transformer (Layer 5), SAEs recover spatially localized features matching a European heatwave (KAN-SAE Δc=2° vs LIN-SAE best match 51°) and a typhoon (both 3°). Steering along the F590 decoder direction warms the European forecast by +1.42 K at α=2, with a linear dose-response (r²>0.99).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse dictionary features recoverable from non-language transformers (weather models) correspond to physical phenomena and act causally on outputs.

fits_no_version.finding: A per-feature B-spline encoder activation gives more alive features (95.2% vs 55.5%) and lower activation-series correlation (median |r| 0.076 vs 0.092) than a ReLU SAE. This comes at a 2.4-point loss in explained variance (84.2 vs 86.6%).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE dictionary quality (dead features, redundancy) depends on the encoder nonlinearity; this bears on SAE methodology, not on superposition itself.

record.problems: Evidence is limited to one model and Layer 5, and to two climate phenomena. The paper itself says generalisation to other models, layers, and phenomena remains to be shown; it also notes that the alive-feature threshold lacks a principled criterion. No uncertainty estimates are reported for the principal comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: None of the claim-bearing reported results were left out. Reconstruction-fidelity and mean-activation-norm comparisons were omitted because they do not measure a claim version.

untested.parts: All of it: no toy models, no sparsity transition, no feature-direction geometry.
All of it: no test of neuron polysemanticity or capacity allocation.
All of it: polysemantic neurons are not studied.
LLMs are not studied. Features spread across neurons are not measured. SAE recovery is shown only in a weather transformer.
Completeness, stability across seeds or sizes, and canonicity of SAE features are not tested.
Whether features are 1-D or multi-dimensional is not tested. The B-spline nonlinearity concerns encoder gating; decoder directions remain 1-D.

record.verdict_notes: This is a method paper by a single author, posted as a preprint, with no uncertainty estimates and one model, layer and SAE size. Interpretable features were chosen by ranking spatial concentration, so the case studies are selected examples. The alive-feature criterion for KAN-SAE (control-point magnitude threshold τ) differs from the 'ever activated' criterion used for LIN-SAE. This weakens the 975 vs 566 comparison.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, feature co-activity sparsity, and the predicted direction geometry are not tested. The paper measures correlations between SAE feature activation time series, not the geometry of underlying feature directions.
The paper does not test whether neuron polysemanticity results from competition for limited capacity or whether important features receive dedicated dimensions.
The paper does not study polysemantic neurons or alternative causes of polysemanticity.
Tests SAE feature recovery in one weather model, not in LLMs; does not measure features spread across neurons.
Does not test SAE feature completeness, stability, or canonical status.
Uses scalar SAE latents and decoder directions but does not test whether the model's underlying features are one-dimensional rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE feature utilisation on held-out test days
rows.note: Reports the number and fraction of alive features in the SAE dictionaries.
rows.check: This compares the study's own method (KAN-SAE) against a linear SAE. Alive-feature rate is a property of the dictionary-learning method, not evidence on V4. The subject is also a weather transformer, not an LLM.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE dead-feature rates on held-out test days
rows.note: The paper also states that L IN -SAE has a median of 1 active day per feature across 53 test days, versus 51 of 53 days for KAN-SAE.
rows.check: Same issue as r1: a dead-feature rate comparing the study's own method with its baseline, in a non-LLM model.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Compared pairwise absolute correlations of feature activation time series
rows.note: This measures correlation of activation time series, not orthogonality or overlap of underlying feature directions.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Compared the fraction of strongly correlated feature pairs
rows.note: A reduction in activation-series correlation does not by itself test the claimed feature-direction geometry.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Identified and compared SAE features matching the European heatwave
rows.measure: Distance of feature activation peak from event centre
rows.baseline: Best matching L IN -SAE feature: displaced by 51°
rows.note: The paper reports that F590 is concentrated over western Europe and overlaps the Z500 positive anomaly of the blocking anticyclone.
rows.check: This is a case study of SAE feature recovery in a weather transformer, not the LLM setting V4 names. The features were selected by ranking spatial concentration, and the LIN-SAE baseline is only a 'best match'. It belongs under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Identified and compared SAE features matching Typhoon Mangkhut
rows.measure: Distance of feature activation peak from storm centre
rows.note: Both methods place a matching feature within 3° of the storm centre; the paper says KAN-SAE has tighter spatial concentration across typhoon test days.
rows.check: Same issue as r5: a non-LLM system. Both SAEs localize the typhoon within 3°, so this row does not separate the methods.

rows.subject: S ONNY
rows.operation_detail: Added a scaled F590 decoder direction to Layer-5 residual activations and passed them through remaining layers
rows.value: +1.42 K; hotspots exceeded +3 K over France and the Iberian Peninsula
rows.note: The study also reports a near-perfectly linear dose-response with r2 > 0.99. This is a causal steering result, not a test of SAE feature completeness or canonical status.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
